text: You guess Claude already knows every matter you have all blended together. It doesn't. By default, it stays inside just this one. Let's see when that changes. Here, Claude has a matter workspace skill, and it sounds like every matter you've ever discussed folds into one shared pool Claude can draw from anytime. But open a brand new matter and ask Claude about specifics from a different case, it can't see them. By default, matter workspace keeps every matter walled off from every other one. Here's what a skill actually is, one file. Matter workspace is a folder holding a single skill, MD plain language instructions Claude reads before it

Works on a matter, no hidden logic. The file is the program. Claude reads that file step section and works through it in order linear, no branching unless a step itself says to branch. And here's the constraint worth knowing. By default, matter workspace never reads across matters. It only draws on another case once cross matter context is switched on in the practices Claude MD. So, matter workspace never gave Claude one shared pool across every case. It just guarantees that every time it runs, Claude reads that same file and stays inside the matter it's pointed at unless that one switches on. Watching Claude answer correctly inside just one matter doesn't prove it's blind

To every other case. Cross matter context might already be switched on. And Claude missing a detail from another matter doesn't prove isolation is working. It might simply not have been asked. A matter workspace skill doesn't blend your cases into one pool. By default, it stays inside the matter it's pointed at, and it only reads across matters once the practice turns that on in Claude MD. Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Read the matter workspace skill and tell me, by default, can you see anything from my other matters? Then tell me exactly what would have to change and where for that to happen. Claude matter workspace Liam in for
